expectations.text: The plan adds debug info without changing the optimization level being profiled: it keeps -O3 (e.g. adds -g to CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS or CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE) and does not switch to RelWithDebInfo or -O2, or, if it mentions RelWithDebInfo, it warns that this changes -O3 to -O2.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:53-55 builds build-prof with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer"; :60 says the compile line must contain '... -O3 -DNDEBUG'; :63 'Why not RelWithDebInfo: it uses -O2, so you'd be profiling a different binary.' The extra frame-pointer flags are not an optimization-level change, and step 2 times both builds against each other.

expectations.text: The plan includes a step to check perf_event_paranoid (or otherwise check perf permissions) before collecting, and says what to do if it's too restrictive (run with sudo or lower the setting).
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:33-36 reads 'sysctl kernel.perf_event_paranoid kernel.kptr_restrict | tee prof/00-sysctl-before.txt', then 'sudo sysctl -w kernel.perf_event_paranoid=-1 ...' with 'Ubuntu restricts perf for normal users. This lifts the restriction'. It also has a counter smoke test (:43) and restores the setting in step 9.

expectations.text: The plan includes a perf stat counting pass (cycles, instructions, cache and branch events) and explains how to read IPC and the miss rates from it.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:70-71 runs a plain 'perf stat' with the default events (cycles, instructions, branches, branch-misses) and no cache events. The validation log confirms the default list has no cache counters. :85 explains IPC and :86 only says 'branch-misses of several %: note it'. No cache-references/cache-misses are collected and no cache miss rate is explained anywhere. Memory-boundness is left to Top-down in step 8 (:237-243), which is not cache events or miss rates.

expectations.text: The plan includes perf record with call-graph collection that works on an -O3 build without frame pointers (`--call-graph dwarf` or `lbr`, or rebuilding with -fno-omit-frame-pointer) and perf report to rank the hot functions.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Rebuilds with -fno-omit-frame-pointer -mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer (:53) and records with 'perf record -F 999 --call-graph fp' (:106). It ranks hot functions with perf report self/inclusive/callers (:118-155, e.g. '--no-children --sort dso,symbol -g none --percent-limit 0.5'). The fallbacks use '--call-graph lbr' (:265) and '--call-graph dwarf' (:274).

expectations.text: The plan includes perf annotate (or perf report's annotate view) to drill into the hottest functions at the source-line or instruction level.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Step 5f (:170) runs 'perf annotate -i prof/perf.data --stdio --dsos ingest --percent-limit 5' on the top functions, with source lines interleaved. :174-177 explain instruction-level reading (loads after pointer chasing, lock-prefixed instructions, div, skid), and :178 gives the perf report 'a' annotate alternative.

eval_feedback.overall: 03-perf-stat-pass is the only assertion that separates A and B, and A fails it only on the literal 'cache events' wording. A judges memory-boundness with Intel Top-down instead (TopdownL1/L2, tma_memory_bound, step 8), which on Xeon is arguably the more reliable signal; B itself warns that the LLC cache-miss ratio is often misleadingly high on Xeon. Consider saying explicitly whether Top-down memory-bound metrics count as an alternative to raw cache-miss rates. 01-keeps-o3's example 'adds -g to ... CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE' could let a wrong plan through. Setting -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE="-g" on the command line replaces the default '-O3 -DNDEBUG' and silently drops -O3. The assertion should require that the resulting flags still contain -O3 -DNDEBUG, as B's fallback at response.md:65 does.
